queue.what: Put the DSpark DRAFT path on the existing dscratch.h arena. dspark_main_kv, dspark_attn_forward, dspark_block_forward, dspark_forward_head and dspark_main_x all call raw cudaMalloc/cudaFree plus a real cudaStreamSynchronize per invocation, once per verify round. The verify path has been on the arena since F44; the draft path predates it and never got it.
queue.expected: +5 to +7%. MEASURED TARGET, not modelled: 10.19 ms/round = 7.4% of the 137.35 ms cycle is HOST time inside cudaMalloc/cudaFree, 134 calls at 76 us, and 127 of the 134 run after their own function's cudaStreamSynchronize -- on a drained, idle GPU. The 12.99 ms of sync (9 calls at 1.44 ms) is NOT priced as waste; it is mostly the host awaiting real draft work.
queue.falsify: In order. (1) LIFETIME: dspark_main_kv runs OUTSIDE the for(pass) loop that calls arena_reset(), so mkv[st] must survive a reset -- audit every buffer that crosses one. This is the way the change can be silently wrong, and it shows as WRONG TOKENS, not a crash, so gate on the byte-identical spec sequence. (2) CAPACITY: the draft adds ~5 MB/round (logits 2.59 MB, bias 517 KB, res2 327 KB, kv_all = ctx*HEAD_DIM*4) against a 512 MB arena; the arena ABORTS on overflow and that kills a 15-minute run, so print g_arena_hwm. (3) Keep the raw path behind an env flag and price it on the nine PAIRED per-verify times at identical K, not on tok/s alone.

queue.what: FP4 for MLA/dense weights -- moves the byte floor ~1.2x but violates 'no additional quantisation'. Needs an explicit decision from the operator to relax the constraint.

Second research phase. Seven queries, axes A/B/C/D/E/F (F twice), all appended to RESEARCH_LOG.md section 2 with outcomes. ZERO promotions -- every hit was already shipped here (FlexDraft's confidence-gated verify length IS our adaptive width, F49/F59/F63), already retired here with a number (tree speculation; grouped GEMM at 1.9x slower; persistent megakernel at 1.05x), or blocked by a standing constraint (MXFP4 the dense path; 4-bit KV; relaxed-lossless). Three are now recorded with the arithmetic that kills them: L2 persistence is dead at 500x (24 MB persistable window against a 12-19 GB re-read distance), llama.cpp's MXFP4 GEMV runs at ~10% of peak against our ~72%, and SubSpec-class quantised self-drafters attack draft COST.
queue.falsify: Per RESEARCH_LOG section 5 this is the FIRST of the two consecutive empty phases that define 'done'. But it was not wasted: two independent 2026 sources (TaxBreak 2603.12465, arXiv 2605.30571) name host/launch-side overhead as the leak in batch-1 decode, this project had measured that on its VERIFY half (F46, 1.05x) and never on its DRAFT half, and reading the draft path for that reason produced F82.

negative_results: THE RESEARCH PHASE, in full: seven queries, six axes, ZERO promotions. FlexDraft/AdaEAGLE adaptive verification length is our adaptive width (shipped F49/F59/F63). OPT-Tree/SpecBranch/CAS-Spec are tree speculation (retired here on a measurement). Fused-MoE/grouped-GEMM is the token-dimension class, degenerate at M=1 and 1.9x slower here. AND THE NULL WAS THE USEFUL PART. Two sources independently name host/launch-side overhead as the batch-1 decode leak; F46 had measured that on the VERIFY (1.05x) and nobody had ever asked it of the DRAFT. That is what got read, and it is a 7.4% lever.

pivot_criterion.why: S5 (draft-head re-alignment) is a TRAINING job the autonomous loop cannot do. Kernel work and training compete for the same operator attention, so the loop must say plainly when kernel work has stopped paying rather than grinding sub-1% levers forever.
pivot_criterion.trigger: PIVOT when open_nontraining_levers == 0 on TWO consecutive audits, OR when three consecutive cycles adopt nothing >=1%. Either fires -> the auditor writes a PIVOT banner to FLYWHEEL_AUDIT.md and creates FLYWHEEL_PIVOT.
pivot_criterion.note: ONE, and it is measured rather than argued: B10, +5 to +7%, from evidence/specprof_f82.log -- 10.19 ms/round of raw cudaMalloc/cudaFree host time on a drained GPU, 7.4% of the spec cycle, in five draft functions that predate the arena the verify has run on since F44. The queue-empty arm needed TWO consecutive audits at 0; it got one (cycle 16) and this cycle RESETS it. The other arm (three consecutive cycles with no >=1% adoption) stays fired and is a correct reading -- nothing has been adopted since F74. The distinction matters: the loop is not out of levers, it is out of ADOPTIONS, and cycle 16's 'the kernel queue is empty' was counted honestly against a map that omitted 17.4% of the cycle. B8'' (~0.4%) and B1 (0.3-0.5%) remain sub-1% and still do not count. S5 and S7 need training. B5 needs the no-additional-quantisation constraint relaxed. B9 is prefill.

position_at_definition.reading: The remaining kernel headroom is ~30% and is spread across many sub-1% items; the acceptance multiplier alone is worth 1.4x. When the kernel queue empties, the pivot is not a defeat -- it is the point where the larger lever becomes the only lever.
